name: The Body Cast (working name)
promise: Your organs, cells and microbes as a cast of characters, arguing about what really happens inside you, in under a minute.
audience: Adults and older teens 16-40 who watch Kurzgesagt, SolarBalls, Zack D. Films. Written for adults: never 'made for kids'.

benchmarks.study: Personified objects with fixed personalities; 'X vs Y' and 'what happens if' titles.
Body and survival topics; 'How X works' titles.
Flat vector look; one surprising number per Short.

voice.name: Felix (Fish Audio library, Australian male)
voice.notes: Fish free tier: 50 requests/day across ALL channels. One request per paragraph, cached by hash. Narrator is Felix; each cast member gets its own voice in 'cast[].voice' once chosen. Launch format: Felix narrates every sourced fact; cast lines are typeset speech bubbles (no second voice). Revisit a voiced cast after ~20 episodes using retention data.

library.spotlight: hook, versus matchups, verdicts, the loop ending

rules: Frame 1: the Spotlight set with the matchup title and both characters already on screen (no build-up).
Cut to the topic's home set for the explanation; change set or camera every 3-5 s.
The speaking character fills at least 35% of the frame height.
Bright subject on a deep or saturated ground; never a pale background.
End on the Spotlight set so the loop back to frame 1 is seamless.
New sets (lungs, kidneys, skin, bone marrow) are added to the library as topics need them, built in studio/stylelab/sets.js first.

script.tone: Narrator deadpan; characters exaggerated but every fact they say is sourced. Health claims: no advice, no cures.
rules: One idea per line. Short sentences. Deadpan: state absurd facts plainly and let the gap carry the joke.
Line one is the hook: the most surprising true sentence in the episode, under the word limit, no preamble.
Spell numbers the way they are spoken ('nineteen thirty-two', 'ten thousand'). Put the digits in the captions.
Every line with a fact, number, name or date cites dossier claim ids. Jokes may not smuggle in new facts.
Estimates and self-reported numbers carry their label on screen (e.g. 'the major's own count').
The last line calls back to the hook or loops into it, so a replay feels intentional.
Use 'gap' (seconds of silence after a line) for comic timing: 0.4-0.6 s before a punchline.
Every line has a speaker from the cast.
Health: describe how the body works; never give medical advice. Prefer NIH, NHS, WHO, peer-reviewed reviews.

radar: New peer-reviewed findings covered by two reputable outlets
Seasonal hooks (flu season, daylight saving, holidays and food)
avoid: Anything that reads as medical advice

sources.notes: Health claims need a primary or official source; journalism alone is not enough.

open_decisions: Character designs: approved in style (Flat Cast); final sheet per character before the first episode
